title: Hiding Hand
equation: Project Survival = Adaptive Creativity ÷ Naive Ambition
hook: If I'd known how hard this would be, I never would've started. Honestly, glad I didn't know.
statement: Underestimating how hard something is can push you into the creativity that actually gets it done.
explainer: Plenty of great projects only happened because someone lowballed the difficulty. Once you're in, you improvise. Just make sure your problem solving keeps pace with your ambition.
sop: Pick one ambitious project you've been avoiding because it feels too hard.
Break it into checkpoints so a failure is survivable.
Score Naive Ambition and Adaptive Creativity from 1 to 10.
If ambition is way ahead of creativity, shrink the next stage.
Write down every workaround you invent along the way.
equation_example: Naive Ambition 8, Adaptive Creativity 6. 6 ÷ 8 = 0.75. Near or above 1 means you're figuring it out as fast as problems show up. Well below 1 means your ambition is outrunning you.
question: Name one worthwhile project you'd never start if you knew exactly how hard it was.
closing_statement: Sometimes not knowing is what gets it built.
